x: With Ken Miller and Alan Black in the first four after half a mile and Cyril Forey and Mike Heck backing up well, our team chances looked very reasonable.

Most improved runners of the season are at present Ken Miller, Alan Black and, Junior Cyril Forey; but perhaps there are some dark horses waiting for the final run-in before they show their hand---Mike Heck, Jim Radford, David Jones and John Thresher for example.
Cyril Forey (a great prospect) was a comfortable winner of the Junior race with John Thresher third; and our Youth success was due to Hampshire and Fairclough being 2nd and 3rd.

Cyril Forey was only 10 yards down on reaching the brook, but fell heavily, enabling John to get well clear. Cyril and Mike Heck made a great effort to close the gap but on reaching the woods they lost sight of John and unwittingly went off course.
After a false start in the Southern, John Thresher and Cyril Forey fell back from 25th and 60th to 95th and 96th, leaving Mike Heck to carry our colours up front and finish 25th.
The most encouraging run of the day was that of Cyril Forey who showed what a great prospect he is by finishing 5th in 29:22 in his first crack at the event!

STAGE 7 - Cyril Forey (19.01, 10th fastest). Cyril is a relatively new member of Belgrave and one of our brightest prospects; a lad who gets fit very quickly, has a good judge of pace and can be a champion if he makes up his mind to stick to the hard work needed to take him to the top.
The team comprised George Piddington, Don Newell, Cyril Forey & Ron Langheim. The Army, who were past the post first, were disqualified, and Woodford failed to finish.
C. Forey · 4:24.8
Lower down the field John Davies and Cyril Forey were running together - the former running within his obvious capabilities, the latter short of training and feeling his way carefully.

STAGE 12 - Cyril Forey (17:50. 2nd fastest) Cyril set off on the last stage into Brighton with the gap ahead still over two minutes. He nevertheless put in an excellent run which gave him 2nd fastest time of the day and we arrived in Brighton in the 6th position we had held since the half-way mark.

Chris Steer led our men home in 57th place, closely followed by Tony Fairclough. Eric Penny 127th and an under-trained Cyril Forey 178th completed our team. We shall do much better in this Championship in future years.

Cyril Forey was making a welcome return to the team on the Gatwick leg. He had the unenviable task of trailing Mick Firth on this windswept stage and it was only towards the end of the leg that Firth's greater experience and fitness took him away from Cyril.
